name: nucleo-h745zi-q
comment: A Nucleo-144 board carrying a STM32H745, built against the STM32H7 sources and linked for this part's memory. Programmed through the ST-LINK already on the board.

flash.comment: 1 MB, flash bank 1: the Cortex-M7's half in the vendor's linker script for this board, bank 2 being the Cortex-M4's. Flash and RAM as the vendor's linker script for this part gives them: vendor/STM32CubeH7/Projects/NUCLEO-H745ZI-Q/Templates/BootCM7_CM4Gated/STM32CubeIDE/CM7/STM32H745ZITX_FLASH.ld

ram.comment: 128 KB of data TCM, where the stack and the data live, as in the vendor's linker script for this board

flash.command: openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -f target/stm32h7x.cfg -c "program {binary} verify reset exit"
flash.comment: Flashing reaches the part through the ST-LINK, which every Nucleo-144 board carries

CONSOLE_TX.comment: Connected to the ST-LINK virtual COM port

supply.comment: A -Q Nucleo-144 board supplies the core from the part's SMPS directly, which is what the vendor's own project for this board defines (USE_PWR_DIRECT_SMPS_SUPPLY, vendor/STM32CubeH7/Projects/NUCLEO-H745ZI-Q/Templates/BootCM7_CM4Gated/STM32CubeIDE/CM4/.cproject). The CMSIS system file leaves Run* mode according to this define, and a supply configuration that does not match the board's wiring stops the part on its first access to flash or locks its supply configuration.
